subject: Clarify output ownership and evaluation usage in MSA / Order Form
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@novum.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Green <michael.green@novum.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify output ownership and evaluation usage in MSA / Order Form

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team has started a pass on the MSA + Order Form and surfaced two areas we need to lock down before procurement can move forward: output ownership and whether Redwood may use customer-generated outputs or snippets for internal evaluation / model improvements.

High level asks from Novum:
- Confirm whether outputs produced by your models (user prompts + generated content) will be owned by Novum, and if so, whether Redwood will assert any rights to use those outputs.
- If Redwood requests rights to use outputs for "product improvement" or "research/evals", we need the scope narrowed (e.g., anonymized, aggregated telemetry only or explicit opt-in).
- Examples of the exact wording Novum can expect for an Order Form carveout or a limited feedback license.

I've attached our MSA redline (Novum_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf) with comments on section 5.3 (Data and Output). Can you please share Redwood's standard language for output ownership / training use, plus any optional language (opt-in vs opt-out approaches)?

We'd like to keep momentum—can we aim for a short call with legal next week if needed?

Best,
Sara
Sara Holt
Head of Legal, Novum AI

Attachments: Novum_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@novum.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify output ownership and evaluation usage in MSA / Order Form

Sara—

Thanks for the clear note and the redline. Appreciated. High-level position from Redwood:

- We do not claim ownership of customer outputs. Customers retain title to outputs generated from their inputs.
- Redwood requests a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback/evaluation license to use short de-identified snippets for model evaluation and quality monitoring only. This would explicitly exclude using customer data to train the public models unless the customer provides an affirmative opt-in.
- Telemetry and aggregated usage metrics (latency, token distribution, error rates) are permitted for SLO/ops purposes; those will be treated separately from any evaluation snippets.

To keep things moving, I'm CC'ing Laura (Legal) to propose three contract-ready options (opt-in, limited eval license, ops-only). If useful, we can do a 30-minute legal-to-legal sync early next week.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Novum MSA redline — need contract language options for outputs / evals

Team—

Looping you in on Novum's redline (attached by their legal head). They want certainty on (1) who owns outputs, and (2) whether Redwood can use outputs or snippets for model evaluation / product improvements. They explicitly highlighted section 5.3 in their draft.

Quick ask: can Legal + Product provide 2–3 contract language options we can present to Novum next week? Preferably:
- Option 1 (Preferred): Customer owns outputs; Redwood may use de-identified, short snippets (<= 200 characters, no PII) only for offline evaluation and quality monitoring. No training or model improvements unless explicit opt-in.
- Option 2 (Customer-friendly opt-in): Customer owns outputs; Redwood may request opt-in for training; default is no training. If customer opts in, provide clear scope (timebound, dataset controls, ability to revoke).
- Option 3 (Ops-only): Customer owns outputs; Redwood may retain logs for SLO/debugging but no eval snippets or training rights.

Also: please identify any compliance traps (PII re-identification risk, telemetry retention limits, EU data residency implications). Novum is US-based but has EU customers and wants clarity for both.

Attachments: Novum_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf (from Novum), I put a stub of a proposed clause in output_clause_proposal.txt—feel free to iterate.

Thanks—Marissa

Subject: Re: Novum MSA redline — need contract language options for outputs / evals

Marissa / team—

Thanks — saw the redline. I drafted three concise options below; I recommend pushing Option A as the initial compromise. I also pasted suggested contract language you can drop into the Order Form / MSA redline.

Summary (pick one to present):

Option A (Recommended):
- Customer retains title to all outputs produced by the Service.
- Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use de-identified, short snippets (not to exceed 200 characters per snippet) of Customer outputs solely for the purpose of offline evaluation, model quality assurance, and regression testing. Redwood will not use such snippets to further train or improve models used in customer-facing or public offerings without an explicit written opt-in from Customer.

Option B (Opt-in Training):
- Customer retains title to outputs.
- Redwood may request the Customer to opt in for additional training use. Any opt-in must be explicit, time-limited, and revocable. If opted in, training datasets will be de-identified and subjected to the agreed data handling protocols in Appendix A.

Option C (Ops-only):
- Customer retains title.
- Redwood may retain logs and aggregated telemetry for operational purposes (SLOs, debugging, billing) but will not retain or use output snippets for evaluation or training.

Proposed clause (Order Form / MSA):
"Customer Output and Feedback License. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Outputs generated by the Service in connection with Customer Data. Subject to the terms below, Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use de-identified, short snippets of Outputs solely for offline evaluation, model quality assurance, and regression testing. Such snippets shall not exceed two hundred (200) characters each and shall exclude any information reasonably likely to identify an individual or contain Customer Confidential Information. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models used for Customer-facing or public offerings without Customer’s explicit written opt-in. Telemetry and aggregated usage metrics necessary for operation, billing, and SLO monitoring are excluded from this license and may be retained under Redwood’s data retention policy as further described in Appendix B."

Compliance notes:
- EU considerations: if Novum routes EU customer traffic via EU regions, we cannot export unredacted EU personal data out of region. For snippets, add an explicit statement that any snippet must be de-identified and processed in-region where required.
- Retention: recommend a maximum retention window for snippet storage (e.g., 90 days) and separate retention for SLO telemetry.
- PII risk: provide an engineering checklist for automated PII filtering + manual review for edge cases.

Next steps:
1) Marissa: share Option A + proposed clause with Novum legal and ask if they prefer opt-in language instead.
2) Ben/Priyom: can you validate the 200-char limit is implementable in our eval pipeline and draft the telemetry retention language for Appendix B?
3) I'll prep a clean redline to send to Novum.

I'll attach the text file with the clause. If Novum pushes back we can escalate to a short legal-to-legal call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
